title.source: Section check: AI in daily life
title.back: Section check: AI in everyday life
title.note: The section's Indonesian title from course.json.

intro.source: 8 questions about Lessons 9–12. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 8 questions about Lessons 9–12. No need to hurry. You may look at the lessons again and try again as often as you like.

questions.0.question.source: A water office now has a machine read the forms that clerks used to type. Which word fits?
questions.0.question.back: A water office now uses a machine to read the forms that office clerks used to type. Which word fits?

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Exposure means a tool could do some tasks in a job. Here, the machine already does the work. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Exposure means a tool could do some of the tasks in a job. Here, the machine already does the work. Look at Lesson 9 again.

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Training means lessons that teach people new skills. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Training means lessons that teach people new skills. Look at Lesson 9 again.

questions.0.options.2.text.note: “Automate” (a verb) → “Otomatisasi” (automation, a noun and a glossary form of Lesson 9's “mengotomatiskan”), so the three options are all nouns and the correct one is not clearly the longest (“Mengotomatiskan” was 15 letters against 12).

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. To automate is to make a machine do work that people used to do.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. Automation means making a machine do work that people used to do.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.note: “To automate is …” → “Otomatisasi berarti …” (automation means …), to match the option.

questions.1.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. Bea works at the front desk of the made-up Northport Clinic. She answers the phone, books visits and helps people who feel worried. Now a new tool books most of the visits.
questions.1.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. Bea works at the front desk of the made-up Northport Clinic. She answers the phone, arranges appointments and helps people who feel worried. Now a new tool arranges most of the appointments.
questions.1.stimulus.body.note: “books visits” → “mengatur janji temu” (arranges appointments), the everyday Indonesian for booking at a clinic.

questions.1.question.source: Based on Lesson 9, what is most likely to happen to Bea's job?
questions.1.question.back: Based on Lesson 9, what is most likely to happen to Bea's job?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: It changes, and she does other tasks
questions.1.options.0.text.back: Her job changes, and she does other tasks

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The tool does one task. People are still needed for others, like helping worried people.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. The tool does one task. People are still needed for other tasks, like helping people who are worried.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: The tool now does every part of her job
questions.1.options.1.text.back: The tool now does every part of her job

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The tool books visits, but it does not help worried people. Tools often do some tasks, not a whole job. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The tool arranges appointments, but it does not help people who are worried. Tools often do some tasks, not a whole job. Look at Lesson 9 again.

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The tool now does one of her tasks, so her work changes. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The tool now does one of her tasks, so her work changes. Look at Lesson 9 again.

questions.2.question.source: Bangkok is a big city. Why does it help when AI sorts the reports?
questions.2.question.back: Bangkok is a big city. Why is it useful when AI sorts the reports?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: It means the city needs no workers
questions.2.options.0.text.back: It means the city does not need workers any more

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. People still check each report and fix the problem. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. People still check each report and fix the problem. Look at Lesson 10 again.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: It gets each report to the right office
questions.2.options.1.text.back: Each report reaches the right office

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. A big city has many offices. Sorting sends each report to the one that should deal with it.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. A big city has many offices. Sorting sends each report to the office that should deal with it.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: It makes every repair free for the city
questions.2.options.2.text.back: Every repair becomes free for the city

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A bigger job may need money and a plan. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A bigger job may need money and a plan. Look at Lesson 10 again.

questions.3.question.source: In 2022, Traffy Fondue won a Thai government award. What does the prize show?
questions.3.question.back: In 2022, Traffy Fondue won an award from the Thai government. What does the award show?
questions.3.question.note: “prize” and “award” are both “penghargaan” here, as one thing is meant.

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A prize shows that officials valued it. It does not show how many problems were fixed.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. An award shows that officials valued it. An award does not show how many problems were fixed.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: How many problems it helped to fix
questions.3.options.1.text.back: How many problems were successfully fixed

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A prize does not count repairs. It shows that officials valued the platform. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. An award does not count repairs. An award shows that officials valued the platform. Look at Lesson 10 again.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: That every report was fixed in time
questions.3.options.2.text.back: That every report was fixed on time

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Bangkok says about 79% were resolved, not all. A prize does not show this. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Bangkok says about 79% have been resolved, not all of them. An award does not show this. Look at Lesson 10 again.

questions.4.question.source: In the study in Nigeria, students did better on an English test. What do the researchers say led to this?
questions.4.question.back: In the study in Nigeria, students got better results in an English test. According to the researchers, what caused this?

questions.4.options.0.text.source: The AI tool, working all on its own
questions.4.options.0.text.back: The AI tool alone, working by itself

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Trained teachers were in the room too. The researchers say the whole programme mattered. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Trained teachers were in that room too. The researchers say it was the whole programme that made the difference. Look at Lesson 11 again.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.note: “the whole programme mattered” → “seluruh program itu yang berpengaruh” (it was the whole programme that had the effect).

questions.4.options.1.text.source: Extra lessons with no computers at all
questions.4.options.1.text.back: Extra lessons with no computers at all

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The students used an AI chat tool in computer rooms. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The students used an AI chat tool in computer rooms. Look at Lesson 11 again.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: The tool and the teachers together
questions.4.options.2.text.back: The tool and the teachers together

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Teachers started each session and helped students stay on task. The tool and the teachers worked together.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. The teachers started each session and helped students stay focused on the task. The tool and the teachers worked together.

questions.5.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. Dani and Kofi practise maths with a made-up homework helper. Dani asks for a hint, then solves each problem himself. Kofi asks for the full answer every time and copies it. Next week, they both take a test with no tools.
questions.5.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. Dani and Kofi practise maths with a made-up homework helper. Dani asks for a hint, then solves each problem himself. Kofi asks for the full answer every time and copies it. Next week, they both take a test with no tools at all.

questions.5.question.source: Think of the study in Türkiye. Who will likely do better on the test?
questions.5.question.back: Remember the study in Türkiye. Who will likely get a better result in the test?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: Kofi, who copied the full answers
questions.5.options.0.text.back: Kofi, who copied the full answers

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. In Türkiye, full answers became a shortcut. That group did worse on the test alone. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. In Türkiye, full answers became a shortcut. That group got worse results in the test without help. Look at Lesson 11 again.

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. In Türkiye, the hint group did about as well as the books group. The full-answer group did worse.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. In Türkiye, the hint group got about the same results as the books group. The full-answer group got worse results.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: Both will get the very same score
questions.5.options.2.text.back: Both will get exactly the same score

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. In Türkiye, the hint group did about as well as the books group. The full-answer group did worse. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. In Türkiye, the hint group got about the same results as the books group. The full-answer group got worse results. Look at Lesson 11 again.

questions.6.question.source: Face recognition software turns the measurements of a face into a set of numbers. What is this set called?
questions.6.question.back: Face recognition software turns the measurements of a face into a set of numbers. What is this set of numbers called?

questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A database is a large store of information. It can hold many faces. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A database is a large store of information. A database can hold many faces. Look at Lesson 12 again.

questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. A template is a set of numbers saved from a face. It is used to check the face later.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. A template is a set of numbers saved from a face. A template is used to check that face later.

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A match is when the tool estimates that two faces belong to the same person. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A match is when the tool estimates that two faces belong to the same person. Look at Lesson 12 again.

questions.7.question.source: A face search says a person in a video matches a photo in its database. What is this match?
questions.7.question.back: A face search says a person in a video matches a photo in its database. What is this match?
questions.7.question.note: “match” as a noun is Lesson 12's glossary word “kecocokan”.

questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A match is a guess, not proof of who someone is. A wrong match can get someone blamed.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. A match is a guess, not proof of who someone is. A wrong match can get someone blamed.

questions.7.options.1.text.source: Proof of who the person is
questions.7.options.1.text.back: Proof of who the person is

questions.7.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A match can be wrong. It is the software's best guess. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.7.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A match can be wrong. A match is the software's best guess. Look at Lesson 12 again.

questions.7.options.2.text.source: A photo that the phone keeps
questions.7.options.2.text.back: A photo that the phone keeps

questions.7.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A phone usually keeps a template, not a photo. A match is the software's best guess. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A phone usually keeps a template, not a photo. A match is the software's best guess. Look at Lesson 12 again.

results.high.source: Well done. You can see what AI does at work, in a city, at school and with faces, and what people still do.
results.high.back: Very good. You can see what AI does at work, in a city, at school and with faces, and what people still do.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Good work. You answered many questions correctly. Look at the lessons again for the questions whose answers were not quite right, then try again if you want.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 9–12, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Look at Lessons 9–12 again, then try again. You may use as much time as you need.
